ATP induces metacromasia and circular dicroism in the dye, 1,9- dimethyl methylene blue, in aqueous solution, when the dye molecules bind to the fully charged ATP molecule.

(i) the metachromasia induced by ATP in the dye 9-dimethylmethylene blue is the result of aggregation of the dye molecules, (ii) the aggregation of bound dye molecules is initiated by twist in the triphosphate backbone of ATP, and (iii) the conformation of ATP molecule in its native environment, as inferred from PMR and circular dichroic studies, is similar to that of ATP in crystalline disodium salt.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ATP molecule, in dilute aqueal solution, maintains its conformation in the crystalline state and the triphosphate moiety in ATP is twisted in a helical sense.
metachromasia is induced in the dye 9-dimethylmethylene blue by ATP at neutral pH when ATP molecule remains in its fully charged state providing four anionic groups to the dye cation.
ATP is a polyanion of four negative charges and the four anionic sites in ATP are sufficient to induce metachromatic and dichroic states in 1.9-dmethylene blue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conformational state of the triphosphoryl moiety of ATP, in the native environment, is a major determinant of the metachromasia of the dye.
the conformation and charge of ATP molecule are maintained in its native environment, and the binding of the dye to ATP induces metachroism and circular dichroic properties in the bound dyes.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the conformational state of a polyanionic biomolecule in its native environment may be inferred from the induced optical properties of the dye bound to it.
the induction of metachromatic and dichroic properties of a dye by a macromolecular polyanion is a sensitive probe to detect the conformation of the polyanion in its native environment.
the induction of metachromatic and circular dichroic properties of a dye by an ATP molecule is a useful probe to study the state of conformaton of ATP in its natural environment.
